notes.canonicalScope: src/index.css token layer and the THE BUTTON / THE ERROR BANNER / PRIMITIVES sections, src/components/ui.tsx, src/layout/Sidebar.tsx, src/components/CommandIndex.tsx, and the shared page shape (.view-container / .page-head / .page-scroll).
notes.nonCanonicalScope: Legacy per-module class families img-*, ctr-*, wsl-*, pkg-*, compose-* in src/features/docker/components/*, src/features/wsl/components/* and the Packages table. They inherit the tokens and the shared button base but predate the component vocabulary and are being migrated onto it.
notes.frontmatterTheme: Frontmatter colour values are the dark rendition, which is the app default (html[data-theme="dark"]). The light rendition is carried per token below as lightTheme.
notes.supersedes: This record replaces an earlier 'Bound Record' notebook direction that was written but never implemented. PRODUCT.md commits to a developer console with no metaphor and no ornament, which is what the shipped stylesheet is.

bg-base.purpose: The ground under everything, and the frame: rail, titlebar, terminal.

bg-primary.purpose: The page the content sits on, and the ground for inset code.

bg-secondary.purpose: Cards, panels, stat tiles, raised rows, the default button.

bg-tertiary.purpose: Inputs, meter tracks, wells, the active state of a pressed button.

bg-hover.purpose: A control under the pointer, and the lightest surface any text can land on. All contrast is measured here.

border.purpose: The default 1px separation. Does the work a shadow would do elsewhere.

border-light.purpose: Row dividers inside a bordered container.

border-strong.purpose: A control's border on hover, and the edge of an overlay.

text-primary.contrast: 16.9:1 dark, 17.8:1 light, on the main panel

text-tertiary.contrast: 6.1:1 dark (4.95:1 on hover), 5.6:1 light (4.7:1 on hover)

accent.purpose: The app's only accent: primary action, current selection, active tab underline, focus ring, command text.

accent-fill.purpose: Background value of the accent, dark enough that white sits on it at 6.3:1. Never used as small text.

accent-hover.purpose: The hover of a filled accent button, and accent text that has to survive its own tinted ground.

accent-subtle.purpose: Selected row, active segment, highlighted index row. The accent acting as furniture.

success.purpose: An operation that succeeded, a container that is running. State only.

success-subtle.purpose: Ground behind green text. Must survive being applied twice.

warning.purpose: Caution: a restarting container, a meter past 75%, an operation with a side effect.

danger.purpose: Failure, or an action that destroys. State only.

danger-fill.purpose: The solid destructive confirm inside a dialog.

danger-subtle.purpose: Ground behind red text, and the outlined destructive button that opens a dialog.

on-brand.purpose: The foreground of the accent and danger fills, and nothing else.

on-fill.purpose: The foreground of the green and amber fills, where white measures 2.1:1 and fails.

chrome-text.purpose: Text on the rail, titlebar and terminal. Solid, never alpha.

chrome-text-subtle.purpose: Counts and section labels in the frame.

chrome-surface.purpose: The active rail item, and the hover of a ghost button.

chrome-surface-hover.purpose: A frame control under the pointer.

chrome-divider.purpose: Separation inside the frame, and the terminal scrollbar.

titlebar-close.purpose: The host platform's own value. The one place the app speaks Windows instead of itself, and therefore unthemed.

syntax-key.purpose: Top-level keys, and the Windows-path badge.

disk-other.purpose: The non-Docker, non-WSL segment of a disk bar.

disk-free.purpose: The empty remainder of a disk bar.

shadow-ink.purpose: The only black. Cast shadow and overlay scrim only, never a surface, border or text colour.

value.purpose: The one big tabular number on a stat card. One per card, never for prose.

title.purpose: The page title in the pinned head. One per view.

heading.purpose: Prerequisite notices, dialog titles, the index search line.

control.purpose: The working size: buttons, fields, tabs, rail items, segment labels.

label.purpose: Anything that names a group of facts: panel titles, table headers, section and stat labels.

mono.purpose: Commands, IDs, paths, terminal output. Never for emphasis or flavour.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Cards, panels, tables and sections. Depth is tone and hairline, never shadow.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: A barely-there seat for small floating chrome.

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Modal-scale overlays and the Ctrl+K index panel.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Hover and colour changes on controls.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion. Travel is removed; state-carrying opacity pulses are kept, and animations are neutralised by keyframe name rather than by selector.

layout.name: terminal-height
layout.purpose: Floats over the content column; not in its height calculation.

layout.name: window-floor
layout.purpose: Desktop only. There is no mobile context, so responsive behaviour is intrinsic rather than breakpoint-driven.

components.name: Default Button
components.description: The neutral action. Raised ground, hairline, primary text.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 28px; padding: 0 11px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.075)); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--color-bg-secondary, #17181b); color: var(--color-text-primary, #f2f3f5); font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.1s ease, border-color 0.1s ease, color 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn:hover { background: var(--color-bg-hover, #24262b); border-color: var(--color-border-strong, rgba(255,255,255,0.15)); } .ds-btn:active { background: var(--color-bg-tertiary, #1e2024); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one committing action on a surface. Solid indigo, white text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 28px; padding: 0 11px; border: 1px solid var(--color-accent-fill, #4c53c4); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--color-accent-fill, #4c53c4); color: #fff; font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.1s ease, border-color 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-accent-hover, #959ced); border-color: var(--color-accent-hover, #959ced); color: #fff; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Danger-outline Button
components.description: The destructive action that opens a dialog. Deliberately lighter than the solid confirm inside it, because the most dangerous action must be the hardest to trigger.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 28px; padding: 0 11px; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-danger, #f2665e) 26%, transparent); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--color-danger-subtle, rgba(242,102,94,0.13)); color: var(--color-danger, #f2665e); font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.1s ease, border-color 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn-danger-outline:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-danger, #f2665e) 20%, transparent); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-danger, #f2665e) 45%, transparent); } .ds-btn-danger-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: The only search control in the app, and it says one verb.
components.css: .ds-field { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 28px; padding: 0 8px; width: 260px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.075)); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--color-bg-tertiary, #1e2024); transition: border-color 0.1s ease; } .ds-field-icon { color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-field-input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; background: none; border: none; outline: none; color: var(--color-text-primary, #f2f3f5); font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); } .ds-field:focus-within { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); outline-offset: -2px; border-color: var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); }

components.name: Tag
components.description: A state annotation at 11px. Five tones; each takes its own colour, a mix of it for the border, and its subtle alpha for the ground.
components.html: local running restarting exited
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; margin-right: 6px; padding: 1px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.075)); border-radius: 4px; background: var(--chrome-surface, rgba(255,255,255,0.045)); color: var(--color-text-secondary, #a2a9b2); font-family: inherit; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-tag--ok { color: var(--color-success, #4ec26a); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-success, #4ec26a) 28%, transparent); background: var(--color-success-subtle, rgba(78,194,106,0.13)); } .ds-tag--warn { color: var(--color-warning, #e0a63a); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-warning, #e0a63a) 28%, transparent); background: var(--color-warning-subtle, rgba(224,166,58,0.13)); } .ds-tag--danger { color: var(--color-danger, #f2665e); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-danger, #f2665e) 26%, transparent); background: var(--color-danger-subtle, rgba(242,102,94,0.13)); }

components.name: Panel
components.description: A bordered group with an 11px uppercase head and tabular meta. No shadow, ever.
components.html:
Reclaimable4 sources
Docker is holding 41.2 GB. 12.4 GB is safe to remove right now.
components.css: .ds-panel { border: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.075)); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--color-bg-secondary, #17181b); overflow: hidden; } .ds-panel-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 12px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-border-light, rgba(255,255,255,0.045)); } .ds-panel-title { font-family: inherit; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); } .ds-panel-meta { font-size: 11px; color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin-left: auto; } .ds-panel-body { padding: 12px 16px; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--color-text-primary, #f2f3f5); }

components.name: Stat Card
components.description: A label, one big tabular number, and a 3px meter that bands amber at 75% and red at 90%. The number is always stated, because a bar alone is not a reading.
components.html: Disk C:78%204 GB free of 931 GB
components.css: .ds-stat { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 5px; width: 200px; padding: 12px 16px; background: var(--color-bg-secondary, #17181b); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.075)); border-radius: 8px; text-align: left; } .ds-stat-label { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); } .ds-stat-value { font-size: 22px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1.1; color: var(--color-text-primary, #f2f3f5); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-stat-unit { font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); font-weight: 400; margin-left: 4px; letter-spacing: 0; } .ds-stat-track { display: block; height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--color-bg-tertiary, #1e2024); overflow: hidden; } .ds-stat-fill { display: block; height: 100%; width: 100%; transform: scaleX(0.78); transform-origin: left; background: var(--color-warning, #e0a63a); } .ds-stat-sub { font-size: 11px; color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Command Block
components.description: The product thesis as a component: the exact command, in the machine's own face, selectable, shown before anything runs.
components.css: .ds-cmd { padding: 12px 16px; } .ds-cmd-label { display: block; font-family: inherit; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); margin-bottom: 6px; } .ds-cmd-code { display: block; font-family: "Cascadia Mono", "Cascadia Code", Consolas, ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 13px; color: var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); background: var(--color-bg-primary, #111214); padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; user-select: text; }

components.name: Tab Strip
components.description: Underline tabs with real tablist semantics: roving tabindex, arrow-key traversal, selection following focus.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.075)); } .ds-tab { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 8px 12px; border: none; background: none; color: var(--color-text-tertiary, #8d949e); font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; margin-bottom: -1px; transition: color 0.1s ease, border-color 0.1s ease; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--color-text-primary, #f2f3f5); } .ds-tab--active { color: var(--color-text-primary, #f2f3f5); border-bottom-color: var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Rail Item
components.description: One module in the flat rail. The active item takes the frame wash and carries aria-current.
components.css: .ds-rail { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1px; width: 212px; padding: 8px; background: var(--color-bg-base, #0b0c0e); } .ds-rail-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 30px; padding: 0 10px; width: 100%; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: var(--chrome-text-muted, #a2a9b2); font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.1s ease, color 0.1s ease; } .ds-rail-item:hover { background: var(--chrome-surface, rgba(255,255,255,0.045)); color: var(--chrome-text, #f2f3f5); } .ds-rail-item--active { background: var(--chrome-surface, rgba(255,255,255,0.045)); color: var(--chrome-text, #f2f3f5); } .ds-rail-label { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-rail-count { font-size: 11px; color: var(--chrome-text-subtle, #8d949e); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-rail-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c84e8); outline-offset: -2px; }

narrative.overview:
This is a developer console held to the craft level of Linear, Vercel and Raycast, and that is a deliberate choice over an authored visual metaphor. The product's name is cartographic and its language is cartographic, but the interface carries no map, no notebook, no ornament. Familiarity is the feature: a developer arrives mid-incident with a full disk or a container that will not start, and they should trust the interface on sight rather than decode it. The tool disappears into the task.

The consequence is that the interface is almost entirely greyscale. Five near-neutral grounds with the barest cool cast, three weights of text, hairline borders, and exactly one accent that carries the primary action, the current selection and the focus ring. Everything else that has colour has it because the machine is in a state: green succeeded, amber is caution, red failed or will destroy. If a colour is not saying one of those things, it does not belong on the screen. Dark is the default because the scene is a developer at their desk beside a dark terminal, often at night; light is a true neutral, never a warm paper.

Density is a design position, not an accident. The whole app runs at 11 to 13px with a 28px control height and 34px table rows, because the user is comparing forty images or six distros and wants them on one screen. That density is what makes contrast and focus visibility structural rather than cosmetic: every colour token in the stylesheet carries its measured contrast ratio in a comment beside it, checked against the lightest ground it can land on rather than the average case, and the focus ring is enforced globally because at 11px there is nothing else to see it by.
keyCharacteristics: Near-neutral greys, one indigo accent, and colour otherwise reserved for state.
Separation is a 1px hairline and a small tone shift. Cards do not float.
Four radii, none of them large; the biggest is 10px and belongs to overlays.
Seven space steps on a 4px scale, and seven type steps, six of which render.
Every number that sits in a column is tabular.
Contrast is measured and recorded in the token comment, not estimated.

rules.name: The Two Accents Rule
rules.body: accent is the text and border value; accent-fill is the background value. Never use the bright accent as a fill under white, and never use the fill accent as small text.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red encode state and nothing else. They are never chrome, never a section accent, never a brand colour. If a colour is not saying "this succeeded / take care / this failed", it is not one of these three.

rules.name: The Fill Names Its Foreground Rule
rules.body: Every filled surface names its own text colour. A single on-brand white fails badly on the bright state colours (white on dark-theme amber measures 2.1:1), so green and amber fills take on-fill and only the accent and danger fills take white.

rules.name: The Solid Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chrome text tokens are solid hex, never alpha. A translucent chrome value composites down against whatever is behind it and fails at 11px.

rules.name: The Doubled Tint Rule
rules.body: A state colour has to survive its own tint applied twice: a selected card takes the subtle ground and the badge inside it takes the same ground again. That doubled ground is the darkest surface either can land on, and it is where the light-theme green and red were re-measured to 4.67:1 and 4.56:1.

rules.name: The One Black Rule
rules.body: shadow-ink is the only black, and it exists for cast shadow and the scrim behind an overlay. It is unthemed, because a shadow is an absence of light in both renditions. The single exception is titlebar-close, the Windows system close-button red.

rules.name: The Annotation Palette Rule
rules.body: Compose files, Dockerfiles and .env are marked up in the app's own syntax-* tokens rather than an imported editor theme, and both themes read the same token names so there is no per-theme override to drift.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace means the string came from the machine or can be pasted back into it. Nothing is monospace for flavour.

rules.name: The Aligned Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number that sits in a column takes font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Sizes, counts, versions, percentages and durations all line up.

rules.name: The Group Label Rule
rules.body: A panel title, a table header and a section label are all 11px, 600, uppercase, 0.06em, tertiary. They are the same thing wearing the same clothes. Do not introduce a fourth treatment for naming a group.

rules.name: The Flat Rail Rule
rules.body: The module list is flat and always will be. Sections within a module live in the in-view tab strip; individual objects live in the index (Ctrl+K). The rail has to take twelve modules as easily as it takes three, which a nested tree cannot.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: A card, panel, table or section gets no shadow. If a thing needs a shadow it is not on the page, it is over the page, and it should be a real overlay with a scrim.

rules.name: The One Exception
rules.body: The 20px titlebar mark is the single place in the app off both scales: a 10px literal on the stylesheet's only gradient. It is a logotype rather than type, exempt under WCAG 1.4.3, and it is the exception that should stay one.

dos: Do build new surfaces from src/components/ui.tsx. If the vocabulary lacks something, add it there.
Do give every view the same three-part shape: pinned head, optional tab strip, one scrolling body.
Do keep spacing on the seven-step 4px scale and pick one of the seven type steps and one of the four radii. All three scales are closed.
Do state a number as well as drawing it. Every meter prints its reading; every reclaim figure prints its size.
Do record the measured contrast ratio in a comment beside any new colour token, against the lightest ground it can land on (bg-hover), not the average case.
Do give any filled surface its own explicit foreground token.
Do show the exact command in a command block wherever the app is about to touch the machine.
Do make anything that switches panels a real tab strip via TabList / Tab, and anything that navigates a rail item with aria-current.
Do label every icon-only control with the row it belongs to, not just its verb: "Remove volume pgdata", not "Remove".
Do keep state-carrying pulses alive under reduced motion, and neutralise animations by keyframe name.
donts: Don't reach for the legacy img-*, ctr-*, wsl-*, pkg-* or compose-* class families in new work. They inherit the tokens but not the vocabulary, and they are being migrated out.
Don't hardcode a colour, size, radius or spacing literal. Every value in this system is a token.
Don't use green, amber or red for anything that is not state.
Don't put a shadow on a card, panel, table or section. Shadows belong to real overlays only.
Don't introduce a radius above 10px, or use full on anything but the status pill and small dots.
Don't use monospace for emphasis or flavour. It means the string came from the machine.
Don't define a chrome text colour as an alpha value. It composites down against the frame and fails.
Don't nest the rail. Sections go in the tab strip, objects go in the index.
Don't ship a search control with a verb other than "Search", or a second empty-state or prerequisite treatment.
Don't suppress a focus ring. The global ring is deliberate and load-bearing at these type sizes.
Don't add ornament that illustrates the atlas metaphor. The metaphor governs language and information architecture; the interface stays a console.
